3.  Authorize the Purchase of a New Isuzu NRR Utility Truck with Switch-N-Go Flatbed and
  Dump Bed System
  The Public Works current large flatbed utility truck is a 2006 Ford LCF model truck, and
  is no longer functioning due to several engine and transmission issues. After evaluating
  available options, City Staff identified the 2024 Isuzu NRR truck with the Switch-N-Go
  system as a cost-effective and practical solution for addressing multiple departmental
  needs with a single, adaptable vehicle.
  Recommended Action
  1. Authorize City Manager, or their designee, to purchase a 2024 Isuzu NRR with Switch-
  N-Go flatbed and dump bed system from Freeway lsuzu located in Corona, CA. 2. Amend
  the budget to increase the Vehicle Replacement Fund (13825-6781) by $15,000 to
  allocate funds for the procurement of the vehicle in the amount not to exceed $125,000.

4.  Purchase of Pump for Pebbly Beach Lift Station
  A pump at Pebbly Beach Lift Station has failed. The Pebbly Beach sewage lift station
  utilizes three pumps. The City’s wastewater treatment plant operator recommended a
  pumps is replaced.
  Recommended Action
  1. Authorize City Manager, or their designee, to purchase Flygt 6” 3OHP submersible
  pump from Xylem Water Solutions, Inc. for the Pebbly Beach sewage lift station for a not
  to exceed sum of $38,500 from Sewer Fund 10850-6521. 2. Make the affirmative finding
  that the Xylem Water Solutions, Inc. has satisfied the sole source requirement as
  specified in the Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4.111(b).

5.  Wet Spot Lease Amendment
  On October 4, 2024, City Staff received a request from Grayce Upton representing The
  Wetspot Rentals be allowed to sublet a section of the outdoor storefront space to Catalina
  Adventure Tours. The space would be used exclusively for the sale of tickets for
  excursions from October to May.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize an amendment to the lease agreement between the City of Avalon and The
  Wetspot Rentals granting expansion of use for city-owned lease property at 120 Pebbly
  Beach Road to allow for occasional sub-letting to Catalina Adventure Tours for ticket
  sales.

PUBLIC HEARING

6.  A Public Hearing Considering a Conditional Use Permit, Variance, Site Plan, and Coastal
  Development Permit to Allow the Demolition of a Vacant Three-Story Apartment
  Building and Construction of a New Four-Story Hotel with Employee Housing in the
  Special Commercial (SC) Zone. (PC#2842)
  On October 22, 2024, the City Council held a duly noticed public hearing to consider
  Appeal No. 24-02, an appeal of the Planning Commission approval of PC#2842. After
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

  consideration of the appeal application, analysis provided in the staff report, applicant
  response, and public comment, the City Council voted 5-0 to set the matter as a de novo
  hearing at the next available regular meeting. The City Council provided direction to Staff
  on specific issue items to be addressed for the de novo hearing for the Project.
  Recommended Action
  1. Open the Public Hearing. 2. Receive public comment. 3. Close the Public Hearing. 4.
  Find the project qualifies for streamlined review under the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15332 (Class 32 In-Fill Development
  —

  Projects. 5. Adopt the findings to support approval of a Conditional Use Permit. 6. Adopt
  the findings to support approval of a Variance. 7. Adopt the findings to support approval
  of a Site Plan. 8. Adopt the findings to support approval of a Coastal Development Permit.
  9. Find the project consistent with the 2024 Annual Growth Policy.

GENERAL BUSINESS

7.  Letter of Understanding with PERC Water Corporation for Operations, Management,
  Maintenance, and Monitoring of the City of Avalon Wastewater System
  The City Council authorized the assignment of the remaining term of an agreement to
  PERC Water Corporation for the operation, management, maintenance, and monitoring
  of Avalon’s Wastewater System. Also, the City Council authorized the City to negotiate a
  contract extension with PERC Water for an additional three year term. City Staff began
  negotiating an additional term in the first half of 2024. The current agreement with PERC
  expires on December 15, 2024. Additional time is needed negotiate a new agreement.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to execute a letter of understanding with PERC Water
  Corporation to continue the maintenance and operations of the City of Avalon’s
  Wastewater System for a 6-month period at a 3% CPI adjusted rate.

5.  Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Miscellaneous Fee Schedule Revisions
  1. City Council heard a presentation regarding the Miscellaneous Fee Schedule.
  2. Mayor Marshall opened the Public Hearing, no comments were made. 3.
  Mayor Marshall closed the Public Hearing. 4. Adopted the fee schedule as
  proposed and adopted Resolution No. 24-39 of the City Council of the City of
  Avalon Setting Fees for Services, Facilities and Activities of the City of Avalon for
  Fiscal Year 2024-25.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Yesenia De La Rosa.
  (All Ayes)

6.  Appeal of Planning Commission Action No. 24-08 of PC#2842 Approving a Site
  Plan, Conditional Use Permit, Variance and Coastal Development Permit at 301
  Beacon Street
  1. Mayor Marshall opened the Public Hearing. 2. Public Comments were heard.
  3. Mayor Marshall closed the Public Hearing. 4. City Council considered the
  appeal and selected option: d) To set the matter for hearing before itself,
  considered de novo (Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Section 9-8.601).

  The de novo hearing will be scheduled for the November 5, 2024 City Council
  meeting. City Council has requested that the applicant/developer Mike Flynn
  provide a complete set of plans (site plan, floor plan, elevation, etc.), edit
  language to reflect that the rooftop deck is to be used for hotel guests and is not
  intended for the general public, and to provide designated parking and loading
  area options (i.e. on-street parking, curb-cut parking, and/or off-street parking).

  Motion to approve made by Lisa Lavelle, seconded by Mary Schickling.
  (All Ayes)

GENERAL BUSINESS

7.  Coyote Joe’s Outdoor Patio Lease Assignment
  Authorized the assignment of the lease for city-owned real property at 113
  Catalina Avenue from Seabring Inc., dba Coyote Joe’s Restaurant to Coyote
  Joe’s Bar and Restaurant, LLC.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Yesenia De La Rosa.
  (All Ayes)

8.  Cabrillo Mole Rehabilitation Phase II Pre-Construction Stage 0
  1. City Council heard a presentation regarding Construction Stage 0 of Phase II
  of the Cabrillo Mole Rehabilitation Project. 2. Authorized the implementation of
  Stage 0 of the Cabrillo Mole Rehabilitation Project including approval of the
  Cabrillo Mole Temporary Facility Plan, four step procurement process,
  administrative procedure for existing tenants at the Cabrillo Mole, and approval of
  the site plan. 3. Made the affirmative finding that the City has made its best effort
  to relocate the tenants at the Cabrillo Mole, and suitable facilities for the Catalina
  Island Company’s ticket booth, Island Enterprises’ ticket booth and storage area,
  Catalina ATM, Inc., and Fish Feeder business cannot be accommodated. 4.
  Delegated authority to the City Manager to negotiate and execute reasonable
  rent agreements with tenants that will be relocated to temporary facilities during
  construction including the Avalon Blue Line Baggage, Catalina Express, Catalina
  Passenger Services (Flyer), and Eli’s Island Deli.
  Motion to approve made by Lisa Lavelle, seconded by Yesenia De La Rosa.
  (All Ayes)

9.  Five Corner Pedestrian Improvements Proect Contract Award
  1. Authorized the City Manager to execute a contract with Jordhal Construction,
  Inc. for the completion of the Five Corners Pedestrian Improvement Project for a
  base scope not-to-exceed sum of $4,737,805. 2. Authorized the City Manager to
  amend the construction contract to approve construction line items once a scope
  of work, to be proportionally reimbursed by third-party entities, is finalized for a
  not-to-exceed amount equal to a reimbursement agreement amount. 3.
  Authorized the City Manager, at his discretion, to amend the construction
  contract to approve additive items for a not-to-exceed sum of $350,000 for
  development items associated with a future workforce housing project.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Lisa Lavelle.
  (All Ayes)

SUBJECT:  Authorize the purchase of a new lsuzu NRR utility truck with
  Switch-N-Go flatbed and dump bed system.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Authorize City Manager, or their designee, to purchase a
2024 Isuzu NRR with Switch-N-Go flatbed and dump bed system from Freeway Isuzu located in
Corona, CA. 2. Amend the budget to increase the Vehicle Replacement Fund (13825-6781) by
$15,000 to allocate funds for the procurement of the vehicle in the amount not to exceed
$1 25,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: The Public Works Department requires dependable and versatile
vehicles to maintain city infrastructure. Our current large flatbed utility truck is a 2006 Ford LCF
model truck, and is no longer functioning due to several engine & transmission issues. Ford
no longer makes parts for this model truck making it very difficult, if not impossible, to repair.
This truck was previously approved for surplus back in September. After evaluating available
options, City Staff identified the 2024 Isuzu NRR truck with the Switch-N-Go system as a cost-
effective and practical solution for addressing multiple departmental needs with a single,
adaptable vehicle.

The 2024 Isuzu NRR truck was selected for its reliability, fuel efficiency, and compatibility with
the Switch-N-Go system. The Switch-N-Go system is a detachable body system that allows
operators to interchange various bed types, including a flatbed and a dump bed. This capability
is essential for our operations, enabling efficient transport of materials, debris, and equipment.
Key benefits of this truck include:

  •  Versatility: The Switch-N-Go system provides adaptability for different jobs, reducing
  the need for multiple vehicles.
  •  Cost Savings: By utilizing one vehicle with multiple bed configurations, the department
  can streamline its fleet, reducing fuel and maintenance expenses.
  •  Efficiency: Rapid bed interchange capabilities will decrease downtime between tasks,
  allowing Public Works staff to respond promptly to maintenance and operational needs.

Quotes were obtained from three lsuzu dealerships located in Southern California based on a
chassis only version of the truck that includes the Switch-N-Go bed system. The following table
shows the proposed cost per truck, which includes taxes and delivery fees. Freeway Isuzu was
the only dealership that can install the Switch-N-Go system in-house. The other two
dealerships must send the truck to a secondary service to install the Switch-N-Go system, both
of which use a company called Enoven. Freeway Isuzu’s proposal was substantially less since
they can install the system in-house This fulfills the purchasing procedure requirements under
 AMC Section 3-4.106 (a). Staff is requesting authority to purchase the truck at a not to exceed
cost of $125,000, which includes the cost of barge fees to ship the truck to the island.

wastewater infrastructure, and any operational downtime can lead to serious consequences,
including potential public health risks and environmental concerns. Recently one of the pumps
has failed, and needs to be rebuilt. The Pebbly Beach sewage lift station utilizes three pumps,
and at peak times of sewer flow, two pumps are required to meet the demand. The third pump
is on standby, and is used if one of the other two pumps fail. PERC Water, our contracted
wastewater treatment plant operator, recommended that one of the pumps get replaced with
a new 3OHP unit, and the second pump be rebuilt to be used as a spare.

Xylem Water Solutions, Inc., a sole source vendor for this pump, provided an estimate of
$33,920. Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Section 3-4.106 requires purchases of goods,
services, supplies and equipment with a value over $25,000 be procured by competitive
procedure. However, AMC Section 3-41 11(b) allows the City to dispense with bidding if there
is only one source for the procurement, or when the City makes the determination that the
purchase can be made more economically and/or efficiently without bidding procedures. In this
case, Xylem is the exclusive supplier of Flygt pumps in our region.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Infrastructure reliability and safety.

FISCAL IMPACTS: A cost not to exceed of $38,500. Sufficient funds exist in FY 24-25 Sewer
Fund 10850-6521.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: An additional pump
failure could lead to potential sewage overflow.

The Class 32 reflects a determination by the California Office of Planning and Research (OPR)
that projects that meet the Class 32 criteria will not have a significant environmental effect and,
therefore, are exempt from CEQA. (Berkeley Hillside Preservation v. City of Berkeley (2015) 60
Cal.4th 1086, 1102.) To apply, a project must be an in-fill development and meet the following
criteria: (1) is consistent with the applicable General Plan designation and applicable policies,
as well as applicable zoning designations and regulations, (2) would occur on a site less than

significant traffic, noise, air quality, or water quality effects, and (5) the site can be adequately
served by all required utilities and public services. The Class 32 exemption reflects the
understanding that “the majority of private projects for which a government permit or similar

circumstances, have little or no effect on the public environment.” (Pacific Palisades Residents

the criteria and qualifies for the Class 32 exemption, the project is categorically exempt from
CEQA unless one of the exceptions to exemptions apply. The exemption is not limited to any
use type and may apply to residential, commercial, industrial, public facility, and/or mixed-use
projects.

Variance:

AMC Chapter 9-8.405 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Variance as
follows:

  6
 1. Variances from the terms of the Zoning Ordinance shall be granted only
  when, because of special circumstances applicable to the property including
  size, shape, topography, location or surroundings, the strict application of
  the Zoning Ordinance deprives such property of privileges enjoyed by other
  property in the vicinity and under identical zoning classification.

  The urban fabric of Avalon is relatively compact, with approximately 80-90 acres
  of existing development already located within the valley floor and the immediately
  surrounding hillsides. The topography of this area surrounding the project site
  represents a transition point between the “Flats” and the increasingly steep
  hillsides to the south and west. The existing development, a three-story apartment
  building, has been vacant for over 20 years, with no interim uses or redevelopment
  applications.

  The Applicant is requesting multiple variances from the development standards for
  the SC zone, as follows:

  •  Allow building height of 28 feet to 44 feet, with an additional 10 feet for
  the elevator building and accessory service building, where 28 feet is
  allowed.
  •  Allow 85% lot coverage, where a maximum of 80% is allowed.
  •  Allow 348% floor area, where a maximum of 140% is allowed.

  Though the property is of regular size, the sloped topography of the lot is unusual
  compared to the majority of other properties within the SC zone. The majority of
  lots within the Special Commercial zone, and commercial zoning districts in
  general, are located within the “Flats.” As a result, the development standards have
  been written to apply to lots with flat topography, which makes development on the
  project site difficult to accomplish within the parameters of the development
  standards as written.

  For instance, the maximum building height in the SC zone is 28 feet. The municipal
  code definition for building height is “…the vertical distance from the lot's natural
  surface to the highest point of the building.” (AMC Section 9-3.608). Other zones
  in the city, particularly the residential zones, have additional detailed standards for
  measurement of building height (low slope, hillside, steep hillside) that account for
  the topography present within the zone to allow for equitable development of all
  lots. Similarly, development standards for lot coverage and floor area in the SC
  zone have not been tailored to take into the account the slope of the lot and the
  impact it will have on perceived mass and bulk above grade. Therefore, in the case
  of a sloped lot in the SC zone, strict application of the definitions of building height,
  floor area, and lot coverage would mean that the actual buildable area of the lot
  would be substantially less on a sloped lot than a flat lot, which would deprive the
  property of the same development potential compared to other properties within
  the same zone.

  topography that would otherwise deprive the property of the development potential

Project Description

The proposed Cameron Hotel is located on the south-west
corner of Beacon Street and Metropole in the City of Avalon.
The existing structure was originally built in 1923. With the
intention of providing housing for the Cameron family whom
occupied the building for over 30 years. However the existing
building has been vacant for the last 30 years and has fallen
into a serious state of disrepair. Numerous unsuccessful
options have been proposed to the Cameron family relating
to bringing this building back to life. The Cameron family has
entered to an agreement with Hamilton Pacific which will
allow the revival of this site.

Rehabilitation of the existing structure was considered and it
was determined to be infeasible because of the integrity of
the existing structure. plumbing, electrical, HVAC, fires
sprinklers do not meet any of todays building codes and
requirements. Therefore it has been determined to remove
the existing building with a new structure that can provide to
the community uses that are desperately needed.

Currently, Avalon is desperately in need employee housing
for both year round housing as well as daily workforce
housing. This type of housing is a strong component of the
new proposed plan. The financial requirements of the type of
housing has to be partially subsidized by other ancillary uses
and activities.

Transient housing/hotel and support uses for visitors and the
community is also a recommended use, compatible with the
neighborhood and the needed workforce housing use.

The Class 32 reflects a determination by the California Office of Planning and Research (OPR)
that projects that meet the Class 32 criteria will not have a significant environmental effect and,
therefore, are exempt from CEQA. (Berkeley Hillside Preseivation v. City of Berkeley (2015) 60
Cal.4th 1086, 1102.) To apply, a project must be an in-fill development and meet the following
criteria: (1) is consistent with the applicable General Plan designation and applicable policies,
as well as applicable zoning designations and regulations, (2) would occur on a site less than
five (5) acres, (3) the project site must have no habitat value, (4) the project would not result in
significant traffic, noise, air quality, or water quality effects, and (5) the site can be adequately
served by all required utilities and public services. The Class 32 exemption reflects the
understanding that “the majority of private projects for which a government permit or similar
entitlement is necessary are minor in scope  ...  and hence, in the absence of unusual
circumstances, have little or no effect on the public environment.” (Pacific Palisades Residents
Association, Inc. v. City of Los Angeles (2023) 88 Cal.App.5th 1338, 1363.) If a project meets
the criteria and qualifies for the Class 32 exemption, the project is categorically exempt from
CEQA unless one of the exceptions to exemptions apply. The exemption is not limited to any
